question: Is the cold-cache arm measurably cold (mincore residency), and what is the decode speed from a verified-cold state?
method: Cold-cache harness with whole-file batched mincore verification (d09d914c): drop -> snapshot (18,363,410 pages, 4096B each) -> COLD/NOT_COLD against 10% threshold, then the standard 2x256 decode. ps-iq2xxs, nmax4, binary SHA 3235529f... unchanged.
readings: 33.27 tok/s first decode from a PROVEN cold state (0 resident pages), 50.75 warm — the 20 tok/s floor holds even verified-cold.
This retroactively validates the earlier advisory-drop arm (115540): its 35.54 tok/s was genuinely a cold-load result; DONTNEED on this file/kernel does evict fully.
Load still only took ~36 s cold (mmap loader faults only what it needs).
limitations: snapshot is not atomic; residency between snapshot and load start could change (nothing else was reading the file)
mincore observes page-cache residency, not GPU L2 or other host caches
